question: A newly created Sentinel incident has no owner or tags. Creation-trigger rule C10 (order 10) adds the tag reviewed. Creation-trigger rule C20 (order 20) assigns an owner only when that tag is present. Update-trigger rule U1 (order 1) was triggered by C10's change and adds a task only when an owner is assigned. Assume no other changes or rules. Which execution outcome follows Sentinel's sequencing rules?

U1 runs between C10 and C20 because C10 triggered it, so no task is added.
C10 and C20 finish before U1; C20 sees the tag, and U1 then sees the owner and adds the task.
C20 evaluates the original untagged incident, so it skips assignment and U1 skips the task.

explanation: Creation-trigger rules complete before update-trigger rules, and each rule evaluates the current incident state.
deepExplanation: Order numbers are local to each trigger queue, not a global priority across both queues. C10's tag is visible to the later creation rule C20. Only after applicable creation rules complete does U1 evaluate the incident, by which time C20 has assigned its owner.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: An update rule's lower number does not place it ahead of the creation-trigger queue.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: A creation rule's update does not interrupt the remaining applicable creation-trigger rules.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: Later rules use the state after earlier actions, not an immutable snapshot of the incident at creation.
